coverage: Reviewed construction/animation cautions, not complete connector profiles. Dimensions below come from installed LDraw part, subpart and primitive records; confirm variant and engagement in each model.

3648a.note: Three keyed axle holes. Only the central hole is the tooth axis. An off-centre mounting is eccentric; do not rotate this part about its origin without identifying the occupied hole.

3650c.note: The crown tooth band is one-sided. Shaft axis is local Z; origin is not the centre of that band. Perpendicular and parallel contact must be assessed separately. A generic coplanar-spur test does not establish a crown mesh.

6575a.note: Choose the occupied axle hole, not the outline centre. Old 6575.dat rotates this part by 180 degrees about Y; compose that transform. A cam follower also needs surface contact and its permitted travel.

3749.note: The same part can be keyed to a gear on its +X end while turning freely in a round support hole on its -X end. Do not rigidly join both neighbours merely because all three axes coincide.

2825.note: End holes are keyed; intermediate pin holes have different mobility. Primitive inference currently also emits male axle features for axlehol4 geometry. Inspect geometry/authored metadata before assigning torque transfer.

6538a.note: Straight keyed coupling; shafts inserted from opposite ends share rotation. Axial retention is a separate requirement.

61903.note: A complete shortcut contains two yokes and a cross. A single rigid object can spin but cannot articulate as a Cardan joint. Split an explicit copy while preserving occurrence identity, colour and rest pose; constrain cross orthogonality and both pivot centres.

77590.note: CV coupling and axial sliding are separate freedoms. Model the mating cup, operating angle, finite insertion and actual shaft lock; a name containing CV does not prove constant speed in an arbitrary assembly.

52731.note: Male CV component, not a complete joint. Pair with the correct cup generation and inspect the seating and permitted articulation.
